articles.title: Is This Open-Source AI Project Still Alive? A 5-Minute GitHub Check Before You Self-Host It
articles.excerpt: I maintain a catalogue of open-source AI projects — 2,155 of them, across 17 categories — and the question I get asked most is not "which tool should I use?" It's "how do I know this project won't be…
articles.body: I maintain a catalogue of open-source AI projects — 2,155 of them, across 17 categories — and the question I get asked most is not "which tool should I use?" It's "how do I know this project won't be abandoned six months after I build on it?" Stars won't tell you. A repository with 40,000 stars can sit untouched for two years. What follows is the five-minute check I actually run, using nothing but the GitHub website. No API keys, no command line. 1. The last commit date — but read it properly Open the repo. Right there on the file list, next to the top file, is the last commit's timestamp. That is your first signal, and it's a blunt one: a last commit from over a year ago is close to a verdict on its own. But a commit from this week means almost nothing by itself.

Claude now joins Google Meet calls as a visible participant, follows the conversation, answers questions out loud or in chat (replies in writing by default), and can draft documents, whiteboards or other artifacts while people are still talking. Notes, transcripts and most in-call answers stay free during the beta; created artifacts are free through 10 February 2027. Support starts on Google Meet for Team and Enterprise plans, with other platforms promised later. It keeps a transcript and screen descriptions, not the raw audio. That is useful for teams that already live in Meet and want an extra participant that can look things up or start a doc.

articles.title: How to Pull Structured Public Data into n8n Without Community Nodes (2 Free Templates)
articles.excerpt: When automating workflows in n8n, bringing in public web data is often where setups become fragile. Custom Puppeteer or Playwright scripts break on site updates, headless browsers consume heavy system…
articles.body: When automating workflows in n8n , bringing in public web data is often where setups become fragile. Custom Puppeteer or Playwright scripts break on site updates, headless browsers consume heavy system memory on self-hosted instances, and custom community nodes can create dependency issues or fail security reviews in production. A cleaner architectural pattern is to decouple data collection from workflow orchestration: let specialized, serverless cloud extractors handle the fetching, parsing, and schema normalization, while n8n handles what it does best: conditional logic, deduplication, and routing data into Google Sheets, Slack, databases, or AI vector pipelines.

articles.body: Query: How have views on Palestine changed over the years? Have parties formed a consensus, and if so has there been any progress towards outcomes? Over the past two decades, parliamentary discourse on Palestine has shifted from broad, low-salience cross-party support for a negotiated two-state solution into sharply polarized debate over formal statehood recognition, international legal accountability, and sanctions. Early 2000s debates framed the issue through traditional multilateral diplomacy, emphasizing United Nations Security Council Resolutions 242 and 338 and the right of both Israel and a self-determining Palestinian state to exist within secure borders [1].

articles.title: Data Leakage Can Make a Customer Churn Model Look Better Than It Is
articles.excerpt: A machine-learning model can produce impressive test results and still fail when it is used on new data. One reason is data leakage: information that would not be available at prediction time has foun…
articles.body: A machine-learning model can produce impressive test results and still fail when it is used on new data. One reason is data leakage : information that would not be available at prediction time has found its way into the training or evaluation process. The model learns from clues about the answer, so its metrics look stronger than its real-world performance. This can happen in ordinary analytics work, often without anyone deliberately doing anything wrong. What leakage looks like Imagine a company wants to identify customers who may cancel next month. The dataset contains customer activity, account details and a churn label. If a feature records the date a customer cancelled, or a status updated after cancellation, it may reveal the outcome directly.

articles.title: I Built My Own Solana Fork. Here's What Actually Happened.
articles.excerpt: I Built My Own Solana Fork. Here's What Actually Happened. I didn't set out to launch a token. I set out to understand what a chain actually is — not in the abstract, but by building one I could boot,…
articles.body: I Built My Own Solana Fork. Here's What Actually Happened. I didn't set out to launch a token. I set out to understand what a chain actually is — not in the abstract, but by building one I could boot, break, and watch finalize in front of me. Machine is the result: a Solana fork with its own genesis, its own token, and a public record of everything it can and cannot do yet. What Machine is Machine runs Agave 2.3.13 — prebuilt release binaries, nothing compiled from source. It boots from a custom genesis I generated, and the genesis hash is published: 32W8ouqrHbuhE3PM6ZsJrJcDbP7Tx9aC2zRvrEabkQSb . The native gas token is $MACHINE. Total supply is 1,000,000,000, distributed at genesis as founder 998,999,000, stake 1,000,000, faucet 1,000.

articles.body: Two decades later, this spectacle from Battlestar Galactica season 3’s “Exodus, Part 2” remains unforgettable sci-fi TV. It’s dazzling and horrifying, and still one of the coolest things ever broadcast on science-fiction television. From a tactical standpoint, the “Adama Maneuver” is absolutely bonkers and one of the riskiest spaceship tactics, perhaps ever (sorry, Vice-Admiral Holdo). articles.body: STARBASE, Texas — SpaceX launched the 15th test flight of its massive Starship rocket today (Nov. 13) and is preparing the vehicle's upper stage for its first-ever return to the launch site in less than 24 hours. Flight 15 lifted off from SpaceX 's Starbase facility here in South Texas at 5:47 p.m. ET (2247 GMT; 4:47 p.m. local Texas time). The towering Super Heavy booster and Ship upper stage cleared the tower without incident and climbed into the skies under more than 18 million pounds of thrust from the booster's 33 Raptor 3 engines. The flight continued nominally through its initial ascent, with the successful execution of Super Heavy's main engine cutoff and Ship's subsequent hot-staging — firing its own Raptors during separation from the booster — about 2.5 minutes after launch.

articles.title: On this day in space! Nov. 13, 1971: NASA's Mariner 9 becomes 1st spacecraft to orbit Mars, revealing close looks at the Martian surface
articles.excerpt: On Nov. 13, 1971, Mariner 9 became the first spacecraft to orbit Mars. Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On Nov. 13, 1971, Mariner 9 became the first spacecraft to orbit Mars. At the time, scientists didn't know much about the Red Planet. NASA had several Mars flybys before Mariner 9 . Those flybys showed that Mars had a cratered surface , so some scientists thought that Mars looked just like the moon. Then Mariner 9 blew blew their minds. When Mariner 9 got to Mars , it arrived in the middle of a dust storm. It saw some tall structures sticking through the clouds. When the dust settled, images from Mariner 9 revealed that these structures were the tops of huge volcanoes. One volcano, Olympus Mons , is the tallest in the solar system. Mariner 9 also spotted an enormous canyon called Valles Marineris . This canyon is five times longer than the Grand Canyon in Arizona.
articles.author: Hanneke Weitering

articles.title: 60 years ago the Leonid meteor shower produced 144,000 meteors per hour. Could it happen again?
articles.excerpt: 60 years ago, the Leonid meteor shower unleashed one of the most spectacular meteor storms in recorded history. As the 2026 peak approaches, here's what skywatchers can expect.
articles.body: This year marks a rather auspicious anniversary for meteor watchers. Sixty years ago , one of the most stupendous Leonid meteor displays lit up the predawn skies over the central and western U.S. So, what will the 2026 Leonids bring us? And what might they bring in the years to come? The Leonid meteor shower is one of the most celebrated of the year's annual displays of "shooting stars." The mere mention of the Leonids usually elicits mental images of a sky filled with shooting stars pouring down through the sky like rain. Such meteor storms have indeed occurred with the Leonids, such as in 1833 and 1966 when meteor rates of tens of thousands per hour were observed.

articles.title: 'Arrival' at 10: Denis Villeneuve's alien visitation classic that reminded us it's good to talk
articles.excerpt: How the 'Dune' director turned a little-known short story into one of the best sci-fi movies of the 21st century
articles.body: In many of the biggest science fiction franchises, conversing with alien races is an absolute doddle. In " Star Trek ", universal translators come as standard, while C-3PO has spent the last 49 years reminding everyone in "Star Wars" that he's fluent in over six million forms of communication. But in "Arrival" — which was released 10 years ago in November 2016 — making first contact proves to be rather more challenging than maintaining your Duolingo streak. In fact, working out how to establish a dialogue with extraterrestrial visitors becomes the whole point of this powerful and heartbreaking story, as the fate of planet Earth hinges on the interpretation of a single noun.

articles.title: Think you have good eyesight? Try counting the stars in the Pleiades tonight
articles.excerpt: Every November, I give myself a completely unscientific eyesight test using one of my favorite sights in the night sky — the Pleiades. How many stars can you see?
articles.body: Every autumn, I conduct an eyesight test that no reputable optometrist would understand. I go outside, find the Pleiades and count how many stars I can see. Usually I start confidently. One, two, three, four, five. Then things become contentious. Is that another star? Did I actually see it, or did I decide I ought to see it because I know it's there? I look away, look back and begin again. This is not, I should emphasize, a meaningful test of eye health. What it tests, rather, is how badly I've prepared for looking at the night sky. The Pleiades sit roughly 444 light-years away in Taurus and are right now becoming extremely convenient in the evening sky. You don't need a telescope to find them. You don't even need binoculars.

articles.title: Windows 0-day dropped by disgruntled researcher hands hackers System rights
articles.excerpt: "SignDrop" exploit lets local users gain all-powerful System rights.
articles.body: Nightmare Eclipse, the pseudonym of a researcher with an ongoing, very public beef with Microsoft, has dropped yet another Windows zero-day. On Tuesday, Nightmare Eclipse disclosed SignDrop, a vulnerability that gives local users full System rights on some versions of Windows. The vulnerability resides in the Common Log File System , which Microsoft describes as a “general-purpose logging service used by software clients running in user-mode or kernel-mode.” By forcing a privileged process such as Windows Defender to open a crafted CLFS container, an attacker with ordinary user rights can abuse the privileged file creation to elevate privileges to System. Turning a Windows defense against itself The attack exploits the interaction of CLFS, Windows Defender, and Windows file permissions.
